findings.evidence: The construct table includes familiar material such as "Button variant contained/outlined/text", "font-*, text-*, space-y-*, gap-*", "aria-label, aria-labelledby, alt" and ":hover, :focus-visible, :active, :disabled". These are predominantly activation cues or standard framework knowledge, unlike the useful version-specific hover, ripple and colorSchemes caveats.
findings.fix: Condense the standard construct inventory to brief activation cues. Retain the framework-specific failure modes, version-sensitive behavior and mappings that prevent non-obvious mistakes; preserve all attribution and source information.

findings.evidence: Workflow line 14 requires a costly-to-undo action to get "a confirm or undo (states)", but the states Rule and Trap contain no confirmation-or-undo criterion. Lines 8 and 132 explicitly say that only the Rule and Trap decide a verdict. A destructive action with otherwise complete request states therefore receives conflicting review instructions.
findings.fix: Add the confirmation-or-undo requirement for costly destructive actions to the states Rule itself, so the build workflow and the closed review criteria enforce the same requirement.

findings.evidence: The a11y Rule begins "Names contain the visible text", but neither that Rule nor its Trap explicitly requires a non-empty accessible name on an icon-only control. Nevertheless, line 121 gives "icon-only IconButton, no accessible name" as a failing-evidence example, and the dashboard eval requires that failure. Under the instruction that nothing outside the Rule and Trap fails a rule, this common case is underspecified.
findings.fix: Start the a11y Rule with an explicit requirement that every interactive control have a non-empty accessible name, including icon-only controls, then retain the requirement that the name contain any visible label text.
